label: Definition of winning
captures: What winning means in this arena, stated so that failing at it is possible.
sufficient_when: A named condition in the market that a competitor could deny them.
not_sufficient: A vision statement any competitor would also sign

label: Winning for whom
captures: The customers and other constituencies in whose eyes the organisation intends to win.
sufficient_when: A specific group is named, not 'the market'.

label: Which customers
captures: The customers in the chosen arena, defined by what they are trying to accomplish and how they choose.
sufficient_when: The definition distinguishes them behaviourally from customers outside the arena.

label: Which offerings
captures: The products, services or categories the organisation will compete with in this arena.

label: Which geographies
captures: The geographic scope of the arena, where geography changes how winning works.

label: Which channels and intermediaries
captures: How the organisation reaches the customer, and who stands between them.
sufficient_when: The channel is named as a choice, with the intermediaries' own interests acknowledged.
note: Frequently the unexamined arena choice; ask even when the user does not raise it.

label: Which stage of the chain
captures: Which activities in the value chain the organisation occupies and which it leaves to others.

label: Where the organisation will not play
captures: The arenas deliberately left to others, including ones the organisation could plausibly have pursued.
sufficient_when: At least one exclusion is something the organisation could have done and someone wanted to do.

label: Insight into the chosen customer
captures: What is understood about why these customers behave as they do in their own context.
sufficient_when: The insight would predict behaviour towards something that does not exist yet.

label: Desired customer action
captures: The specific behaviour the strategy must compel, including both quantity and price.
sufficient_when: An observable action is named, with a sense of how much and at what price.

label: Promise to the customer
captures: What is promised to the chosen customer, in terms they would recognise.
sufficient_when: Valuable to them, memorable at the point of choice, and specific enough that breaking it would be visible.

label: Route to advantage
captures: Whether winning rests on a structurally lower cost position or on difference customers pay for.
sufficient_when: One is chosen, and the trade-offs the other would have required are acknowledged.

label: The winning logic
captures: The causal chain from what the organisation does to why the chosen customer chooses it.
sufficient_when: It reads as a because-therefore chain, not a list joined by 'and'.

label: Why competitors cannot simply copy it
captures: What a rival would have to give up to match this, or why they would be unwilling.
sufficient_when: A trade-off is named, not a secret or a head start.

label: Who else is competing for this action
captures: The named alternatives the customer actually considers, including substitutes and doing nothing.
sufficient_when: Specific alternatives are named and what the customer does today is described.

label: Expected competitor response
captures: What rivals do once this becomes visible, and why that does not neutralise the strategy.

label: Capabilities the logic requires
captures: The activities that must be done distinctively well for the winning logic to hold.
sufficient_when: Each one is traceable to a step in the winning logic.

label: Capability gaps and how they close
captures: Which required capabilities the organisation lacks, and whether each is built, bought, partnered or dropped.

label: How the capabilities reinforce each other
captures: Which capabilities are valuable only in the presence of the others.

label: What changes in the management systems
captures: The measures, budgets, reviews, routines and incentives that change to build and protect the choices.
sufficient_when: At least one concrete change is named that someone would notice next month.

label: Leading indicators
captures: Non-financial measures tied to the conditions the strategy's logic depends on.

label: Who owns which choice
captures: The named owner of each choice and the boundaries within which it is theirs to make.

label: What gets funded and defunded
captures: The actual movement of money, people and senior attention implied by the choices.
sufficient_when: Something is being reduced, not only added.

label: Alternative possibilities considered
captures: The other genuine ways the organisation could have tried to win, and why they were set aside.
sufficient_when: At least one alternative differed in Where-to-Play, not only in emphasis.

label: What would have to be true
captures: The conditions about customers, competitors, capabilities, channels and economics that must hold for this to be a great choice.
sufficient_when: Written as falsifiable statements about the world rather than as intentions.

label: The least believed condition
captures: Which of the must-be-trues the team believes least, and why.

label: Tests for the barriers
captures: The cheapest evidence that would change the team's mind about each barrier, with pass and fail criteria set in advance.

label: What would prove this wrong
captures: The observations, agreed now, that would mean the strategy should change.

label: What is given up
captures: What the organisation becomes worse at, or declines to pursue, as a direct consequence of these choices.
sufficient_when: Someone internally lost something they wanted.

label: The strategy stated plainly
captures: The strategy as the user would say it out loud, without a document.
sufficient_when: It names the customer, the arena, the way of winning, and what is excluded.

label: What changes for functions and units
captures: What a specific function or unit now chooses differently because of this strategy.

label: Who the user is in this work
captures: The person's role in this strategy work and their relationship to the choices - owner, adviser, analyst, or someone trying to influence upward.
sufficient_when: Their role and their relationship to the decision are both clear.

label: Who decides
captures: What this person can decide alone, what they can influence, and who owns anything that is fixed for them.
sufficient_when: For the choices under discussion, the owner is named - whether or not it is the user.
